summary: Attala County, MS tower with an unknown build date; a 1948 fire-danger station was added, and NHLR says the Mississippi Forestry Commission has vacated the site.

facts.design: 100-ft Aermotor LS-40 with straight internal staircase
facts.status_note: Vacated by the Mississippi Forestry Commission per NHLR's 2022 site visit; listed as standing in a 2023 note. No later record found.

events.note: Fire-danger rating station built at the tower by the Mississippi Forestry Commission (Clarion-Ledger, as quoted on Forest Lookouts)
NHLR site visit July 9, 2022; site vacated by the MFC
Listed as standing (Google Earth) on Forest Lookouts list

evidence.supports: purpose of the station: wind speed and humidity for daily fire danger
evidence.quote: the station will provide tower personnel a means of determining the daily fire danger by measuring wind velocity and humidity

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Vacated per the 2022 NHLR site visit; listed as standing in a 2023 note. No record after 2023 was found, so current condition is not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: Build year unknown in every readable source (NHLR says Unknown). The 1948 report is read only through the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes the Clarion-Ledger; the newspaper itself was not read. A second search returned FCC tower #1042132 'Kosciusko, MS (Dismantled)', which is a cellular structure, not this lookout, and was not used. An Attala Historical Society history page (https://sites.rootsweb.com/~msahs/history.html) returned 403 and was not read. Access level omitted: no source readable here states public access. The brief record's access 'unknown' stays.
